kv.memory.confidence-chat-attach-review-: Confidence chat+attach review: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: I did not read kith-store source so I could not verify whether get_changes_since_ordered correctly handles the state format, whether state counters are per-type or global, or whether the Mutex<Store> could deadlock if a store method calls another store method internally. Would raise confidence: reading kith-store/src to verify state counter semantics and that no store method holds a lock while calling another store method.
kv.memory.kith-attach-phase-2-taildrop-t: kith-attach Phase 2: Taildrop (tailscale file send/get) is NOT a substitute for kith-attach. Taildrop has no API surface kithd can drive programmatically, no delivery receipt, and no message threading integration. kith-attach blob storage (stored locally, served over kithd HTTPS, referenced by blobId in JMAP) is the correct approach. Taildrop is useful for interactive user-to-user file transfer only.
kv.memory.kith-peer-complete-delivery-in: kith-peer: complete_delivery in OutboxStore (kith-store) is the atomic success path; mark_delivered is retained only for orphaned-outbox-row cleanup when the message no longer exists. Never use mark_delivered for normal delivery success.
kv.memory.maintainer-risk-for-chat-attac: Maintainer risk for chat+attach review: MEDIUM. Key issues: newState race between lock scopes in all three set handlers; silent destroy ID drop; content-type validation too weak; attachment size/sha256 not verified against actual blob bytes.
kv.memory.spec-design-principle-always-h: spec design principle: always have 2+ very different implementations before finalizing a protocol spec. One implementation writes a spec shaped like itself; diverse implementations force you to find real abstractions vs deployment-specific choices. Kith+nie validated this for the JMAP Chat I-D — forced generalization of topology, identity format, and body encoding.
